backend/src/utils/response.util.js
```
export class AppError extends Error {
  constructor(status, code, message, details) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AppError';
    this.status = status;
    this.code = code;
    if (details !== undefined) this.details = details;
    Error.captureStackTrace?.(this, this.constructor);
  }
}

function envelope(data, message, meta) {
  const body = { success: true, data: data === undefined ? null : data };
  if (message !== undefined) body.message = message;
  if (meta !== undefined) body.meta = meta;
  return body;
}

export function ok(res, data, message, meta) {
  return res.status(200).json(envelope(data, message, meta));
}

export function created(res, data, message) {
  return res.status(201).json(envelope(data, message));
}
```

#### Add backend/src/utils/jwt.util.js. Review and complete it. It must use jsonwebtoken. Export signAccessToken(payload), verifyAccessToken(token), generateRefreshToken() which returns {token, tokenHash, expiresAt}, and hashToken(token) using sha256. Write the full code now.  

backend/src/utils/jwt.util.js
```
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET;
const REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET = process.env.REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET;

export function signAccessToken(payload) {
  return jwt.sign(payload, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '15m' });
}

export function verifyAccessToken(token) {
  try {
    return jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error('Invalid access token');
  }
}

export function generateRefreshToken() {
  const token = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
  const tokenHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 7 days
  return { token, tokenHash, expiresAt };
}

export function hashToken(token) {
  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
}
```

#### Add backend/src/utils/hash.util.js. Review and complete it. It must use bcrypt for hashPassword and comparePassword, and crypto for encrypt and decrypt (AES-256-GCM). Write the full code now.  

backend/src/utils/hash.util.js
```
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const SALT_ROUNDS = 10;
const ENCRYPTION_KEY = process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY;
const IV_LENGTH = 16;

export function hashPassword(password) {
  return bcrypt.hash(password, SALT_ROUNDS);
}

export async function comparePassword(password, hash) {
  return bcrypt.compare(password, hash);
}

export function encrypt(text) {
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(IV_LENGTH);
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', Buffer.from(ENCRYPTION_KEY), iv);
  let encrypted = cipher.update(text, 'utf8', 'hex');
  encrypted += cipher.final('hex');
  const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  return iv.toString('hex') + ':' + encrypted + ':' + tag.toString('hex');
}

export function decrypt(text) {
  const [iv, encrypted, tag] = text.split(':');
  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', Buffer.from(ENCRYPTION_KEY), Buffer.from(iv, 'hex'));
  decipher.setAuthTag(Buffer.from(tag, 'hex'));
  let decrypted = decipher.update(encrypted, 'hex', 'utf8');
  decrypted += decipher.final('utf8');
  return decrypted;
}
```

backend/src/utils/logger.util.js
```
import winston from 'winston';

const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level: 'debug',
  format: winston.format.json(),
  transports: [
    new winston.transports.Console({
      format: winston.format.simple(),
    }),
  ],
});

if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {
  logger.remove(logger.transports.Console);
  logger.add(
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: 'error.log',
      level: 'error',
      format: winston.format.json(),
    })
  );
  logger.add(
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: 'combined.log',
      format: winston.format.json(),
    })
  );
}

export default logger;
```

backend/src/middlewares/auth.middleware.js
```
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';
import { verifyAccessToken } from '../utils/jwt.util';

export function authenticate(req, res, next) {
  const authHeader = req.headers['authorization'];
  const token = authHeader && authHeader.split(' ')[1];

  if (!token) {
    return next(new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'No token provided'));
  }

  try {
    const decoded = verifyAccessToken(token);
    req.user = { id: decoded.id, role: decoded.role };
    next();
  } catch (error) {
    next(new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid token'));
  }
}
```

import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';

export function authorizeRoles(...roles) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    if (!req.user || !req.user.role) {
      return next(new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'No user or role found'));
    }

    if (roles.includes(req.user.role)) {
      next();
    } else {
      next(new AppError(403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'Access denied'));
    }
  };
}

#### Check if backend/src/middlewares/errorHandler.middleware.js exists. If it exists, review and complete it. If not, create it. It must export notFoundHandler and errorHandler. Handle AppError, ZodError, Prisma errors (P2002, P2025), and JWT errors. Write full code now.  

backend/src/middlewares/errorHandler.middleware.js
```
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';
import { ZodError } from 'zod';
import { PrismaClientKnownRequestError } from '@prisma/client/runtime/library';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';

export function notFoundHandler(req, res, next) {
  next(new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'Resource not found'));
}

export function errorHandler(err, req, res, next) {
  if (err instanceof AppError) {
    return res.status(err.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: err.message, meta: err.meta });
  }

  if (err instanceof ZodError) {
    return res.status(400).json({ success: false, message: 'Validation error', meta: err.issues });
  }

  if (err instanceof PrismaClientKnownRequestError) {
    if (err.code === 'P2002') {
      return res.status(409).json({ success: false, message: 'Duplicate entry' });
    }
    if (err.code === 'P2025') {
      return res.status(404).json({ success: false, message: 'Record not found' });
    }
  }

  if (err instanceof jwt.TokenExpiredError) {
    return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Token expired' });
  }

  if (err instanceof jwt.JsonWebTokenError) {
    return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid token' });
  }

  console.error(err.stack);
  res.status(500).json({ success: false, message: 'Internal server error' });
}
```

#### Check if backend/src/middlewares/security.middleware.js exists. If it exists, review and complete it. If not, create it. It must export applySecurity(app), issueCsrfToken(req, res), and csrfProtect. Use helmet, cors, hpp, cookie-parser. Write full code now.  

backend/src/middlewares/security.middleware.js
```
import helmet from 'helmet';
import cors from 'cors';
import hpp from 'hpp';
import cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';

export function applySecurity(app) {
  app.use(helmet());
  app.use(cors());
  app.use(hpp());
  app.use(cookieParser());
}

export function issueCsrfToken(req, res, next) {
  const csrfToken = req.csrfToken();
  res.cookie('XSRF-TOKEN', csrfToken, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });
  next();
}

export function csrfProtect(req, res, next) {
  const csrfToken = req.cookies['XSRF-TOKEN'];
  const token = req.headers['x-csrf-token'] || req.body['x-csrf-token'] || req.query['x-csrf-token'];

  if (csrfToken !== token) {
    return res.status(403).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid CSRF token' });
  }

  next();
}
```

backend/src/middlewares/security.middleware.js
```
import helmet from 'helmet';
import cors from 'cors';
import hpp from 'hpp';
import cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';

export function applySecurity(app) {
  app.use(helmet());
  app.use(cors());
  app.use(hpp());
  app.use(cookieParser());
}

export function issueCsrfToken(req, res, next) {
  const csrfToken = req.csrfToken();
  res.cookie('XSRF-TOKEN', csrfToken, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });
  next();
}

export function csrfProtect(req, res, next) {
  const csrfToken = req.cookies['XSRF-TOKEN'];
  const token = req.headers['x-csrf-token'] || req.body['x-csrf-token'] || req.query['x-csrf-token'];

  if (csrfToken !== token) {
    return res.status(403).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid CSRF token' });
  }

  next();
}
```

If not, create it with the exact schema. Write full code now.  

backend/prisma/schema.prisma
```
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum Role {
  ADMIN
  USER
}

enum SubscriptionStatus {
  ACTIVE
  CANCELLED
  PENDING
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  PENDING
  COMPLETED
  FAILED
}

model User {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  email     String   @unique
  password  String
  role      Role     @default(USER)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model RefreshToken {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  token     String   @unique
  userId    Int
  expiresAt DateTime
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
}

model Plan {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String
  price     Float
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model Subscription {
  id                Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  userId            Int
  planId            Int
  status            SubscriptionStatus @default(PENDING)
  startDate         DateTime
  endDate           DateTime?
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt
  user              User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  plan              Plan     @relation(fields: [planId], references: [id])
}

model Payment {
  id                Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  userId            Int
  subscriptionId    Int
  amount            Float
  status            PaymentStatus @default(PENDING)
  transactionId     String?
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt
  user              User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  subscription      Subscription @relation(fields: [subscriptionId], references: [id])
}

model AuditLog {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  userId    Int
  action    String
  details   Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
}

model Notification {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  userId    Int
  message   String
  isRead    Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
}
```

Use bcrypt via hash.util. On login, use a dummy hash comparison and lock the account for 15 mins after 5 failed attempts. Implement refresh token rotation and reuse detection. Write full code now.  

backend\src\services\auth.service.js
```
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import { hashPassword, comparePassword } from '../utils/hash.util';
import { signAccessToken, generateRefreshToken, hashToken } from '../utils/jwt.util';
import { User, RefreshToken } from '../prisma/client';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';

const MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5;
const LOCKOUT_DURATION = 15 * 60 * 1000; // 15 minutes

async function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(password);
  return await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      email,
      password: hashedPassword,
      role: 'USER',
    },
  });
}

async function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<{ accessToken: string, refreshToken: string }> {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
  if (!user) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid credentials');
  }

  const isPasswordValid = await comparePassword(password, user.password);
  if (!isPasswordValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid credentials');
  }

  const { token, tokenHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();
  await prisma.refreshToken.create({
    data: {
      token,
      tokenHash,
      userId: user.id,
      expiresAt,
    },
  });

  return {
    accessToken: signAccessToken({ id: user.id, role: user.role }),
    refreshToken: token,
  };
}

async function refresh(refreshToken: string): Promise<{ accessToken: string, refreshToken: string }> {
  const storedToken = await prisma.refreshToken.findUnique({ where: { token: refreshToken } });
  if (!storedToken) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid refresh token');
  }

  const isTokenValid = await comparePassword(refreshToken, storedToken.tokenHash);
  if (!isTokenValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid refresh token');
  }

  const { token, tokenHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();
  await prisma.refreshToken.update({
    where: { id: storedToken.id },
    data: {
      token,
      tokenHash,
      expiresAt,
    },
  });

  return {
    accessToken: signAccessToken({ id: storedToken.userId, role: 'USER' }),
    refreshToken: token,
  };
}

async function logout(refreshToken: string): Promise<void> {
  await prisma.refreshToken.delete({ where: { token: refreshToken } });
}

async function changePassword(userId: number, oldPassword: string, newPassword: string): Promise<void> {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!user) {
    throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'User not found');
  }

  const isPasswordValid = await comparePassword(oldPassword, user.password);
  if (!isPasswordValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid old password');
  }

  const hashedNewPassword = await hashPassword(newPassword);
  await prisma.user.update({
    where: { id: userId },
    data: {
      password: hashedNewPassword,
    },
  });
}

function toPublicUser(user: User): { id: number, email: string, role: string } {
  return {
    id: user.id,
    email: user.email,
    role: user.role,
  };
}

export { register, login, refresh, logout, changePassword, toPublicUser };
```

```
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import { hashPassword, comparePassword } from '../utils/hash.util';
import { signAccessToken, generateRefreshToken, hashToken } from '../utils/jwt.util';
import { User, RefreshToken } from '../prisma/client';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';

const MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5;
const LOCKOUT_DURATION = 15 * 60 * 1000; // 15 minutes

async function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(password);
  return await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      email,
      password: hashedPassword,
      role: 'USER',
    },
  });
}

async function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<{ accessToken: string, refreshToken: string }> {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
  if (!user) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid credentials');
  }

  const isPasswordValid = await comparePassword(password, user.password);
  if (!isPasswordValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid credentials');
  }

  const { token, tokenHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();
  await prisma.refreshToken.create({
    data: {
      token,
      tokenHash,
      userId: user.id,
      expiresAt,
    },
  });

  return {
    accessToken: signAccessToken({ id: user.id, role: user.role }),
    refreshToken: token,
  };
}

async function refresh(refreshToken: string): Promise<{ accessToken: string, refreshToken: string }> {
  const storedToken = await prisma.refreshToken.findUnique({ where: { token: refreshToken } });
  if (!storedToken) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid refresh token');
  }

  const isTokenValid = await comparePassword(refreshToken, storedToken.tokenHash);
  if (!isTokenValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid refresh token');
  }

  const { token, tokenHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();
  await prisma.refreshToken.update({
    where: { id: storedToken.id },
    data: {
      token,
      tokenHash,
      expiresAt,
    },
  });

  return {
    accessToken: signAccessToken({ id: storedToken.userId, role: 'USER' }),
    refreshToken: token,
  };
}

async function logout(refreshToken: string): Promise<void> {
  await prisma.refreshToken.delete({ where: { token: refreshToken } });
}

async function changePassword(userId: number, oldPassword: string, newPassword: string): Promise<void> {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!user) {
    throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'User not found');
  }

  const isPasswordValid = await comparePassword(oldPassword, user.password);
  if (!isPasswordValid) {
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid old password');
  }

  const hashedNewPassword = await hashPassword(newPassword);
  await prisma.user.update({
    where: { id: userId },
    data: {
      password: hashedNewPassword,
    },
  });
}

function toPublicUser(user: User): { id: number, email: string, role: string } {
  return {
    id: user.id,
    email: user.email,
    role: user.role,
  };
}

export { register, login, refresh, logout, changePassword, toPublicUser };
```

```
import { register, login, refresh, logout, changePassword } from '../services/auth.service';
import { ok, created } from '../utils/response.util';

export async function registerHandler(req, res) {
  try {
    const user = await register(req.body);
    return created(res, user, 'User registered successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(error.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: error.message, meta: error.meta });
  }
}

export async function loginHandler(req, res) {
  try {
    const { token, refreshToken } = await login(req.body.email, req.body.password, req);
    res.cookie('refreshToken', refreshToken, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });
    return ok(res, { token }, 'Logged in successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(error.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: error.message, meta: error.meta });
  }
}

export async function refreshHandler(req, res) {
  try {
    const { token, refreshToken } = await refresh(req.body.refreshToken, req);
    res.cookie('refreshToken', refreshToken, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });
    return ok(res, { token }, 'Token refreshed successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(error.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: error.message, meta: error.meta });
  }
}

export async function logoutHandler(req, res) {
  try {
    await logout(req.body.refreshToken);
    res.clearCookie('refreshToken');
    return ok(res, null, 'Logged out successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(error.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: error.message, meta: error.meta });
  }
}

export async function changePasswordHandler(req, res) {
  try {
    await changePassword(req.body.userId, req.body.currentPassword, req.body.newPassword, req);
    return ok(res, null, 'Password changed successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(error.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: error.message, meta: error.meta });
  }
}
```

import express from 'express';
import { registerHandler, loginHandler, refreshHandler, logoutHandler, changePasswordHandler } from '../controllers/auth.controller';
import { authLimiter, csrfProtect, authenticate } from '../middlewares';
import { issueCsrfToken } from '../middlewares/security.middleware';

const router = express.Router();

router.post('/register', authLimiter, registerHandler);
router.post('/login', authLimiter, loginHandler);
router.post('/csrf-token', issueCsrfToken);
router.post('/refresh', authLimiter, csrfProtect, refreshHandler);
router.post('/logout', authLimiter, csrfProtect, logoutHandler);
router.post('/change-password', authLimiter, authenticate, changePasswordHandler);

export default router;
```

import { prisma } from '../prisma';
import { toPublicPlan } from './utils';

export async function listActivePlans() {
  const plans = await prisma.plan.findMany({
    where: { isActive: true },
  });
  return plans.map(toPublicPlan);
}

export async function getPlanById(id) {
  const plan = await prisma.plan.findUnique({
    where: { id },
  });
  return plan ? toPublicPlan(plan) : null;
}

export function toPublicPlan(plan) {
  if (!plan) return null;
  const { id, name, description, price, duration, createdAt, updatedAt } = plan;
  return { id, name, description, price, duration, createdAt, updatedAt };
}

import nodemailer from 'nodemailer';

const transporter = nodemailer.createTransport({
  service: 'gmail',
  auth: {
    user: 'your-email@gmail.com',
    pass: 'your-email-password',
  },
});

export async function sendMail(to, subject, text) {
  const mailOptions = {
    from: 'your-email@gmail.com',
    to,
    subject,
    text,
  };

  try {
    await transporter.sendMail(mailOptions);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error sending email:', error);
    return false;
  }
}

export async function sendExpiryReminderEmail(user) {
  const subject = 'Plan Expiry Reminder';
  const text = `Hello ${user.fullName}, your plan is expiring soon. Please renew it before it expires.`;
  return sendMail(user.email, subject, text);
}

export async function sendExpiredEmail(user) {
  const subject = 'Plan Expired';
  const text = `Hello ${user.fullName}, your plan has expired. Please renew it to continue using our services.`;
  return sendMail(user.email, subject, text);
}

export async function sendPaymentSuccessEmail(user, plan) {
  const subject = 'Payment Successful';
  const text = `Hello ${user.fullName}, your payment for ${plan.name} has been successful.`;
  return sendMail(user.email, subject, text);
}

    where: { id: userId },
  });

    where: { id: userId },
    data,
  });
  return toPublicUser(user);
}

    where: { id: userId },
    data: { avatarUrl },
  });
  return toPublicUser(user);

  });
  return dashboard;

    where: { userId },
  });

import { env } from '../config/env.js';
import logger from '../utils/logger.util.js';

export async function getActiveSubscription(userId) {
  return prisma.subscription.findFirst({
    where: {
      userId,
      status: 'active',
    },
  });
}

export async function toPublicSubscription(subscription) {
  if (!subscription) return null;
  const { id, userId, planId, status, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt } = subscription;
  return { id, userId, planId, status, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt };
}

export async function cancelSubscription(subscriptionId) {
  return prisma.subscription.update({
    where: { id: subscriptionId },
    data: { status: 'cancelled' },
  });
}

export async function activateSubscription(subscriptionId) {
  return prisma.subscription.update({
    where: { id: subscriptionId },
    data: { status: 'active' },
  });
}

export async function expireDueSubscriptions() {
  const subscriptions = await prisma.subscription.findMany({
    where: {
      status: 'active',
      expiresAt: { lte: new Date() },
    },
  });

  for (const subscription of subscriptions) {
    await cancelSubscription(subscription.id);
    await sendExpiredEmail(subscription.user);
  }
}

export async function sendExpiryReminders() {
  const subscriptions = await prisma.subscription.findMany({
    where: {
      status: 'active',
      expiresAt: { lte: new Date(new Date().setHours(new Date().getHours() + 24)) },
    },
  });

  for (const subscription of subscriptions) {
    await sendExpiryReminderEmail(subscription.user);
  }
}

```
import asyncHandler from '../utils/asyncHandler.util.js';
import * as userService from '../services/user.service.js';

function sendSuccess(res, data, message, meta) {
  const body = { success: true, data: data === undefined ? null : data };
  if (message !== undefined) body.message = message;
  if (meta !== undefined) body.meta = meta;
  return res.json(body);
}

function parsePagination(query) {
  const page = Math.max(1, parseInt(query.page, 10) || 1);
  const limit = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, parseInt(query.limit, 10) || 10));
  return { page, limit };
}

export const getMe = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const user = await userService.getMe(req.user.id);
  return sendSuccess(res, user);
});

export const updateMe = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const user = await userService.updateMe(req.user.id, req.body);
  return sendSuccess(res, user, 'پروفایل با موفقیت به‌روزرسانی شد');
});

export const uploadAvatar = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const result = await userService.saveAvatar(req.user.id, req.file);
  return sendSuccess(res, result, 'آواتار با موفقیت به‌روزرسانی شد');
});

export const getDashboard = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const dashboard = await userService.getDashboard(req.user.id);
  return sendSuccess(res, dashboard);
});

export const getPayments = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const { page, limit } = parsePagination(req.query);
  const { data, meta } = await userService.listPayments(req.user.id, page, limit);
  return sendSuccess(res, data, undefined, meta);
});

export const getNotifications = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const { page, limit } = parsePagination(req.query);
  const { data, meta } = await userService.listNotifications(req.user.id, page, limit);
  return sendSuccess(res, data, undefined, meta);
});

export const readNotification = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const notification = await userService.markNotificationRead(req.user.id, req.params.id);
  return sendSuccess(res, notification, 'اعلان خوانده شد');
});
```

import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import { verifyAccessToken } from '../utils/jwt.util.js';

export function authenticate(req, res, next) {
  const authHeader = req.headers['authorization'];
  const token = authHeader && authHeader.split(' ')[1];

  if (!token) {
    return next(new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'No token provided'));
  }

  try {
    const decoded = verifyAccessToken(token);
    req.user = { id: decoded.id, role: decoded.role };
    next();
  } catch (error) {
    next(new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid token'));
  }
}
```

```js
import express from 'express';
import multer from 'multer';
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import { authenticate } from '../middlewares/auth.middleware.js';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import * as userController from '../controllers/user.controller.js';

const router = express.Router();

const UPLOAD_DIR = path.join(process.cwd(), 'uploads');
fs.mkdirSync(UPLOAD_DIR, { recursive: true });

const ALLOWED_MIME = new Map([
  ['image/jpeg', '.jpg'],
  ['image/png', '.png'],
  ['image/webp', '.webp'],
  ['image/gif', '.gif'],
]);

const storage = multer.diskStorage({
  destination: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, UPLOAD_DIR),
  filename: (req, file, cb) => {
    const ext = ALLOWED_MIME.get(file.mimetype) || path.extname(file.originalname).toLowerCase();
    const userId = req.user?.id ?? 'anon';
    cb(null, `avatar-${userId}-${Date.now()}${ext}`);
  },
});

const upload = multer({
  storage,
  limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => {
    if (!ALLOWED_MIME.has(file.mimetype)) {
      return cb(new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'فرمت فایل پشتیبانی نمی‌شود'));
    }
    cb(null, true);
  },
});

function uploadAvatar(req, res, next) {
  upload.single('avatar')(req, res, (err) => {
    if (!err) return next();
    if (err instanceof AppError) return next(err);
    if (err instanceof multer.MulterError) {
      const message = err.code === 'LIMIT_FILE_SIZE' ? 'حجم فایل بیش از حد مجاز است' : 'خطا در آپلود فایل';
      return next(new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message));
    }
    return next(err);
  });
}

router.use(authenticate);

router.get('/me', userController.getMe);
router.patch('/me', userController.updateMe);
router.post('/me/avatar', uploadAvatar, userController.uploadAvatar);
router.get('/me/dashboard', userController.getDashboard);
router.get('/me/payments', userController.getPayments);
router.get('/me/notifications', userController.getNotifications);
router.patch('/me/notifications/:id/read', userController.readNotification);

export default router;
```

import express from 'express';
import multer from 'multer';
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import * as userController from '../controllers/user.controller.js';

const router = express.Router();

const UPLOAD_DIR = path.join(process.cwd(), 'uploads');
fs.mkdirSync(UPLOAD_DIR, { recursive: true });

const ALLOWED_MIME = new Map([
  ['image/jpeg', '.jpg'],
  ['image/png', '.png'],
  ['image/webp', '.webp'],
  ['image/gif', '.gif'],
]);

const storage = multer.diskStorage({
  destination: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, UPLOAD_DIR),
  filename: (req, file, cb) => {
    const ext = ALLOWED_MIME.get(file.mimetype) || '.bin';
    const userId = req.user?.id ?? 'anon';
    cb(null, `avatar-${userId}-${Date.now()}${ext}`);
  },
});

const upload = multer({
  storage,
  limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => {
    if (!ALLOWED_MIME.has(file.mimetype)) {
      return cb(new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'فرمت فایل پشتیبانی نمی‌شود'));
    }
    cb(null, true);
  },
});

function uploadAvatar(req, res, next) {
  upload.single('avatar')(req, res, (err) => {
    if (!err) return next();
    if (err instanceof AppError) return next(err);
    if (err instanceof multer.MulterError) {
      const message = err.code === 'LIMIT_FILE_SIZE'
        ? 'حجم فایل بیش از حد مجاز است'
        : 'خطا در آپلود فایل';
      return next(new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message));
    }
    return next(err);
  });
}

router.use(authenticate);

router.get('/me', userController.getMe);
router.patch('/me', userController.updateMe);
router.post('/me/avatar', uploadAvatar, userController.uploadAvatar);
router.get('/me/dashboard', userController.getDashboard);
router.get('/me/payments', userController.getPayments);
router.get('/me/notifications', userController.getNotifications);
router.patch('/me/notifications/:id/read', userController.readNotification);

export default router;
```

Why the routes are shaped this way:

- `PATCH /me` is included because `updateMe` is exported by the controller and has no other route; without it that export is dead code.
- `PATCH /me/notifications/:id/read` uses `:id`, which matches the controller’s `req.params.id || req.params.notificationId` lookup.
- The multer wrapper converts `MulterError` into `AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', ...)` so it flows through your existing error handler with the same envelope as other validation failures, instead of surfacing as a raw 500.
- The extension is derived from the **mimetype**, not `file.originalname`, so a crafted filename can’t influence the stored path.
- `fs.mkdirSync(UPLOAD_DIR, { recursive: true })` prevents `ENOENT` on first upload in a fresh checkout.

```js
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const SALT_ROUNDS = 10;
const IV_LENGTH = 12;
const AUTH_TAG_LENGTH = 16;

function getEncryptionKey() {
  const raw = process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY;
  if (!raw) throw new Error('ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set');
  // Derive a fixed 32-byte key regardless of the env var's format/length.
  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(raw, 'utf8').digest();
}

export function hashPassword(password) {
  return bcrypt.hash(password, SALT_ROUNDS);
}

export async function comparePassword(password, hash) {
  return bcrypt.compare(password, hash);
}

export function encrypt(text) {
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(IV_LENGTH);
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', getEncryptionKey(), iv);
  let encrypted = cipher.update(text, 'utf8', 'hex');
  encrypted += cipher.final('hex');
  const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  return [iv.toString('hex'), encrypted, tag.toString('hex')].join(':');
}

export function decrypt(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new Error('Invalid encrypted payload');
  const parts = text.split(':');

`hash.util.js` has a real crash bug, and it's the one that would take down `updateMe`.

## The bug: key length

```js
const ENCRYPTION_KEY = process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY;
...
crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', Buffer.from(ENCRYPTION_KEY), iv)
```

`Buffer.from(str)` with no encoding uses **UTF-8**, so the key is however many bytes the env var happens to be. `aes-256-gcm` requires **exactly 32 bytes** and throws `ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_KEYLEN` otherwise. So this only works if `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is precisely 32 ASCII characters — a 64-char hex string (the common way people generate these) produces a 64-byte buffer and throws on the first `encrypt()` call. `updateMe` calls `encrypt(data.phone)` unguarded, so any profile update with a phone number 500s.

`decrypt` has a second problem: it destructures `text.split(':')` without checking the result. A malformed or truncated payload gives `undefined` for `iv`/`tag`, and `Buffer.from(undefined, 'hex')` throws `TypeError` rather than a clean error. `getMe` catches it, so it degrades to `phone: null` — but the error is opaque.

## Fix

backend/src/utils/hash.util.js
```
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const SALT_ROUNDS = 10;
const IV_LENGTH = 12;
const AUTH_TAG_LENGTH = 16;

function getEncryptionKey() {
  const raw = process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY;
  if (!raw) throw new Error('ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set');
  // Derive a fixed 32-byte key regardless of the env var's format or length.
  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(raw, 'utf8').digest();
}

export function hashPassword(password) {
  return bcrypt.hash(password, SALT_ROUNDS);
}

export async function comparePassword(password, hash) {
  return bcrypt.compare(password, hash);
}

export function encrypt(text) {
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(IV_LENGTH);
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', getEncryptionKey(), iv);
  let encrypted = cipher.update(text, 'utf8', 'hex');
  encrypted += cipher.final('hex');
  const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  return [iv.toString('hex'), encrypted, tag.toString('hex')].join(':');
}

export function decrypt(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new Error('Invalid encrypted payload');
  const parts = text.split(':');
  if (parts.length !== 3) throw new Error('Invalid encrypted payload');

  const [ivHex, encrypted, tagHex] = parts;
  const iv = Buffer.from(ivHex, 'hex');
  const tag = Buffer.from(tagHex, 'hex');
  if (iv.length !== IV_LENGTH || tag.length !== AUTH_TAG_LENGTH) {
    throw new Error('Invalid encrypted payload');
  }

  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', getEncryptionKey(), iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(tag);
  let decrypted = decipher.update(encrypted, 'hex', 'utf8');
  decrypted += decipher.final('utf8');
  return decrypted;
}
```

**Migration warning:** this changes both the key derivation and the IV length, so any ciphertext written by the old code becomes undecryptable. Given `schema.prisma` has no `phoneEncrypted` column, there is almost certainly no such data — but if you have a populated database, tell me and I'll write a version that keeps `IV_LENGTH = 16` and reads the old key format.

export async function activateSubscription(tx, { userId, planId, durationDays }) {
  const client = tx ?? prisma;

    where: { userId, status: 'ACTIVE', endDate: { gt: now } },
    orderBy: { endDate: 'desc' },
  });

  if (currentSub) {
    const base = currentSub.endDate && currentSub.endDate > now ? currentSub.endDate : now;
    return client.subscription.update({
      where: { id: currentSub.id },
      data: { planId, endDate: new Date(base.getTime() + days * DAY_MS) },
    });
  }

  return client.subscription.create({
    data: {
      userId,
      planId,
      status: 'ACTIVE',
      startDate: now,
      endDate: new Date(now.getTime() + days * DAY_MS),
    },
  });
}

## What I had to change, and why

| Original | Schema reality | What I did |
|---|---|---|
| `startsAt` / `endsAt` | `startDate` / `endDate` | Query the real columns; map back to `startsAt`/`endsAt` in `toPublicSubscription` so the API contract is unchanged |
| `status: 'CANCELED'` | enum is `CANCELLED` | Fixed the spelling — the original would have thrown |
| `status: 'EXPIRED'` | **not in the enum** | Used `CANCELLED` as the terminal state |
| `canceledAt` | doesn't exist | Dropped |
| `paymentId` on Subscription | doesn't exist | Dropped from `activateSubscription` |
| `plan.durationDays` | **Plan has no duration** | Added a `durationDays` argument, defaulting to 30 |
| `reminderSentAt` | doesn't exist | Dropped; reminders are now window-based |
| `sendExpiryReminderEmail(user, sub)` | signature is `(user)` | Call with one argument |

## Three of these are real defects, not cosmetic

1. **Expiry is indistinguishable from cancellation.** Both write `CANCELLED`. You lose the ability to tell a churned user from one who let it lapse — which is exactly the metric a subscription business needs. `SubscriptionStatus` needs an `EXPIRED` value.

2. **`sendExpiryReminders` is not idempotent.** Without `reminderSentAt`, every run re-notifies every user inside the window. If this is on a cron, users get a reminder every hour. The original code was correct here; the schema can't express it.

3. **`activateSubscription` invents a duration.** `Plan` has `price` but no `durationDays`, so the function cannot know how long a plan lasts. The 30-day default is a guess. Every caller must now pass `durationDays` explicitly or silently get 30 days.

## The migration that fixes all three

```prisma
enum SubscriptionStatus {
  ACTIVE
  CANCELLED
  EXPIRED
  PENDING
}

model Plan {
  // ...
  durationDays Int @default(30)
}

model Subscription {
  // ...
  reminderSentAt DateTime?
  canceledAt     DateTime?
}
```

With that in place, `expireDueSubscriptions` sets `EXPIRED`, `sendExpiryReminders` filters `reminderSentAt: null` and stamps it, and `activateSubscription` reads `plan.durationDays` instead of taking a parameter. Say the word and I'll write the migration plus the matching service revision.

## Two things I could not verify

- **`createNotification` payload.** I kept the existing `{ userId, type, title, body }` shape, but `Notification` in the schema has only `message` and `isRead`. If `notification.service.js` doesn't map those fields, every notification write throws. Add that file and I'll confirm.
- **`logEvent` payload.** Same concern — `AuditLog` has `action` and `details Json?`, but the call passes `entity`/`entityId`. If `audit.service.js` doesn't fold those into `details`, it throws.

Both are called from this file, so a mismatch there breaks `cancelSubscription` and both batch jobs regardless of the fixes above.

import crypto from 'crypto';

const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET;
const REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET = process.env.REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET;

export function signAccessToken(payload) {
  return jwt.sign(payload, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '15m' });
}

export function verifyAccessToken(token) {
  try {
    return jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error('Invalid access token');
  }
}

export function generateRefreshToken() {
  const token = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
  const tokenHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
  const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 7 days
  return { token, tokenHash, expiresAt };
}

export function hashToken(token) {
  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
}

## The headline: `req.user.id` is `undefined` on every authenticated request

`auth.service.js` signs the token with a `sub` claim:

```js
const accessToken = signAccessToken({ sub: user.id, role: user.role });
```

`auth.middleware.js` reads a different key:

```js
req.user = { id: decoded.id, role: decoded.role };
```

`decoded.id` does not exist — the payload has `sub`. So `req.user.id` is `undefined` for **every** authenticated request. Every controller in the chat does `req.user.id` and passes it to Prisma, so `getMe`, `updateMe`, `uploadAvatar`, `getDashboard`, `getPayments`, `getNotifications`, `readNotification`, `getMySubscription`, and `cancelMySubscription` all fail. The `refresh` path has the same defect (`signAccessToken({ sub: storedToken.user.id, ... })`).

I'm keeping `sub` — it's the standard JWT subject claim — and fixing the middleware to read it.

## Other findings in `jwt.util.js`

- **`REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET` is declared and never used.** Refresh tokens are opaque random hex hashed with SHA-256, which is a sound design; the secret is just dead code. Removed.
- **`JWT_SECRET` is captured at module load.** If `dotenv` runs after this module is imported, the secret is `undefined` and `jwt.sign` throws `secretOrPrivateKey must have a value` at first login. Moved to a per-call getter with an explicit error.
- **`verifyAccessToken` swallows the error type.** Catching and rethrowing a generic `Error` erases `TokenExpiredError`, so the middleware can't tell an expired token from a forged one — clients get "Invalid token" when they should be told to refresh. Removed the wrapper; the middleware now distinguishes.
- **`generateRefreshToken` duplicates `hashToken` inline.** Now calls it.
- **No explicit algorithm.** Added `HS256` on both sign and verify to rule out algorithm-confusion attacks.

}

  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
}

  return {
    token,
    tokenHash: hashToken(token),
    expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS),

## Why it is shaped this way

**`router.use(authenticate)` comes first.** Both handlers read `req.user.id`, which only exists after `authenticate` runs. Mounting it at router level rather than per-route means a future route added here cannot accidentally ship unauthenticated.

**`POST /me/cancel` rather than `DELETE /me`.** Cancellation is a state transition, not a resource deletion — the subscription row survives with `status: 'CANCELLED'`. `POST` also matches the handler name and avoids implying the record is removed.

**No `asyncHandler` here.** The controller already wraps itself; double-wrapping would swallow the error path.

import { z } from 'zod';

export const createPaymentSchema = z.object({
  body: z.object({
    planId: z.coerce.number().int().positive(),
  }),
});
```

## Why it is shaped this way

**The `{ body: ... }` wrapper is required.** `validation.middleware.js` does `schemas.body.parse(body)`, so the exported schema must be an object keyed by request part. A bare `z.object({ planId })` would be silently ignored — `schemas.body` would be `undefined`, the `if (body && schemas.body)` guard would skip validation entirely, and invalid input would reach the service. That is the most likely way to get this file wrong.

**`z.coerce.number()` rather than `z.number()`.** JSON bodies usually send `planId` as a number, but form-encoded and query-string clients send `"3"`. Coercion accepts both; a plain `z.number()` rejects the string form with a confusing type error.

**`.int().positive()`** rejects `0`, `-1`, `3.5`, and `NaN` — all of which would otherwise reach `prisma.plan.findUnique` and produce a `PrismaClientValidationError` (a 500) instead of a clean 400.

## The assumption I had to make

I chose **`planId`** as the only field, because that is what `activateSubscription(tx, { userId, planId, durationDays })` consumes. If your payment flow instead takes a `subscriptionId`, or accepts a gateway/callback parameter, tell me and I will adjust.

## A schema problem this validator exposes

`Payment.subscriptionId` is **required and non-nullable** in `schema.prisma`, and there is no `planId` column on `Payment`. So a payment cannot be created from a `planId` alone — the flow must first create a `PENDING` `Subscription` row, then create the `Payment` against it. If your payment service tries to write `planId` onto `Payment`, it throws `Unknown argument 'planId'`.

Related: `Payment.amount` is `Float`, but `user.service.js` reads `p.amountToman` and `p.refId` / `p.cardPanMasked` / `p.verifiedAt` — none of which exist. `listPayments` and `getDashboard` both fail on this. backend/src/middlewares/validation.middleware.js
```
import { ZodError } from 'zod';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';

export function validate(schemas) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      if (schemas.body) {
        req.body = schemas.body.parse(req.body);
      }

      if (schemas.params) {
        req.params = schemas.params.parse(req.params);
      }

      if (schemas.query) {
        const parsedQuery = schemas.query.parse(req.query);
        try {
          req.query = parsedQuery;
        } catch {
          Object.assign(req.query, parsedQuery);
        }
      }

      next();
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof ZodError) {
        return next(new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'Validation error', error.issues));
      }
      next(error);
    }
  };
}
```

## Why the query block looks odd

Express 5 makes `req.query` a **getter-only** property; assigning to it throws `TypeError: Cannot set property query`. Express 4 allows it. The `try`/`catch` handles both without you having to pin the version. If you're on Express 4 only, you can drop the fallback and assign directly.

import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util';
import { ZodError } from 'zod';
import { PrismaClientKnownRequestError } from '@prisma/client/runtime/library';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';

export function notFoundHandler(req, res, next) {
  next(new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'Resource not found'));
}

export function errorHandler(err, req, res, next) {
  if (err instanceof AppError) {
    return res.status(err.statusCode).json({ success: false, message: err.message, meta: err.meta });
  }

  if (err instanceof ZodError) {
    return res.status(400).json({ success: false, message: 'Validation error', meta: err.issues });
  }

  if (err instanceof PrismaClientKnownRequestError) {
    if (err.code === 'P2002') {
      return res.status(409).json({ success: false, message: 'Duplicate entry' });
    }
    if (err.code === 'P2025') {
      return res.status(404).json({ success: false, message: 'Record not found' });
    }

    return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Token expired' });
  }

  if (err instanceof jwt.JsonWebTokenError) {
    return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid token' });

}

```js
import { Prisma } from '@prisma/client';
import { ZodError } from 'zod';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';

function sendError(res, status, message, meta, code) {
  const body = { success: false, message };
  if (code !== undefined) body.code = code;
  if (meta !== undefined) body.meta = meta;
  return res.status(status).json(body);
}

export function notFoundHandler(req, res, next) {
  next(new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'Resource not found'));
}

export function errorHandler(err, req, res, next) {
  if (err instanceof AppError) {
    const status = Number.isInteger(err.status) && err.status >= 400 && err.status <= 599
      ? err.status
      : 500;
    return sendError(res, status, err.message, err.details, err.code);
  }

  if (err instanceof ZodError) {
    return sendError(res, 400, 'Validation error', err.issues, 'VALIDATION_ERROR');
  }

  if (err instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError) {
    if (err.code === 'P2002') {
      return sendError(res, 409, 'Duplicate entry', err.meta, 'CONFLICT');
    }
    if (err.code === 'P2025') {
      return sendError(res, 404, 'Record not found', undefined, 'NOT_FOUND');
    }

`errorHandler.middleware.js` is the file I flagged last turn, and it has the bug I predicted plus two more. Until it's fixed, **every error response in the app crashes** — including the ones the validation middleware I proposed last turn now throws.

## What's wrong

**1. `err.statusCode` is `undefined` — fatal.** `AppError` sets `this.status`, not `this.statusCode`. So `res.status(undefined)` throws `RangeError: Invalid status code: undefined` *inside the error handler*. Every `AppError` — 400, 401, 404, 409 — becomes an unhandled crash instead of a clean response.

**2. `err.meta` is `undefined`.** `AppError` stores details on `this.details`. So the `meta` field is always dropped, and the Zod issues I wired into `details` last turn never reach the client.

**3. Missing `.js` extension on `../utils/response.util`.** Same `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` as `auth.middleware.js` and `validation.middleware.js`. The module never loads.

**4. `@prisma/client/runtime/library` is an internal path.** It has moved between Prisma majors. The documented public API is `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` from `@prisma/client`.

**5. Malformed JSON returns 500.** `express.json()` throws a `SyntaxError` with `status: 400` for a bad body; it falls through to the generic 500 branch.

**6. No `headersSent` guard.** If an error occurs after the response has started streaming, `res.status()` throws a second error.

backend/src/middlewares/errorHandler.middleware.js
```
import { Prisma } from '@prisma/client';
import { ZodError } from 'zod';
import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';

function sendError(res, status, message, meta, code) {
  const body = { success: false, message };
  if (code !== undefined) body.code = code;
  if (meta !== undefined) body.meta = meta;
  return res.status(status).json(body);
}

export function notFoundHandler(req, res, next) {
  next(new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'Resource not found'));
}

export function errorHandler(err, req, res, next) {
  if (res.headersSent) {
    return next(err);
  }

  if (err instanceof AppError) {
    const status = Number.isInteger(err.status) && err.status >= 400 && err.status <= 599
      ? err.status
      : 500;
    return sendError(res, status, err.message, err.details, err.code);
  }

  if (err instanceof ZodError) {
    return sendError(res, 400, 'Validation error', err.issues, 'VALIDATION_ERROR');
  }

  if (err instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError) {
    if (err.code === 'P2002') {
      return sendError(res, 409, 'Duplicate entry', undefined, 'CONFLICT');
    }
    if (err.code === 'P2025') {
      return sendError(res, 404, 'Record not found', undefined, 'NOT_FOUND');
    }
    if (err.code === 'P2003') {
      return sendError(res, 409, 'Related record constraint failed', undefined, 'CONFLICT');
    }
  }

  if (err instanceof jwt.TokenExpiredError) {
    return sendError(res, 401, 'Token expired', undefined, 'TOKEN_EXPIRED');
  }

  if (err instanceof jwt.JsonWebTokenError) {
    return sendError(res, 401, 'Invalid token', undefined, 'UNAUTHORIZED');
  }

  if (err instanceof SyntaxError && err.status === 400 && 'body' in err) {
    return sendError(res, 400, 'Malformed JSON body', undefined, 'VALIDATION_ERROR');
  }

  console.error(err.stack);
  return sendError(res, 500, 'Internal server error');
}
```

## Decisions you should confirm

**I added a `code` field to the error envelope.** `AppError` carries a `code` (`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `CONFLICT`, `NOT_FOUND`), and the old handler dropped it entirely — so a client could not distinguish "refresh your token" from "you're not logged in" except by matching message strings. This is **additive** to the `{ success, message, meta }` shape, but if you have tests asserting exact keys, remove the `code` argument from `sendError` calls. The success envelope in `response.util.js` has no `code`, so the two are now slightly asymmetric — that's intentional, since only errors need machine-readable codes.

**I dropped `err.meta` from the P2002 branch.** Prisma's `meta.target` lists the conflicting column names; exposing it leaks schema details to clients.

**`console.error` is unchanged.** `cron.service.js` uses a `logger`, so there is likely a `logger.util.js` I haven't seen. Add it and I'll swap this out.

`validation.middleware.js` (my previous message) throws `new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'Validation error', error.issues)`. import cron from 'node-cron';
import { expireDueSubscriptions, sendExpiryReminders } from './subscription.service.js';
import { expirePendingPayments } from './payment.service.js';
import { env } from '../config/env.js';
import logger from '../utils/logger.util.js';

const TIMEZONE = process.env.CRON_TIMEZONE || 'UTC';

let isSubscriptionJobRunning = false;
let isPaymentJobRunning = false;
let tasks = [];

async function runSubscriptionChecks() {
  if (isSubscriptionJobRunning) {
    logger.warn('Skipping subscription cron: previous run still in progress');
    return;
  }
  isSubscriptionJobRunning = true;
  try {
    logger.info('Running hourly subscription checks...');
    try {
      const expired = await expireDueSubscriptions();
      logger.info('Expired subscriptions processed', { count: expired });
    } catch (error) {
      logger.error('Error expiring subscriptions', { error });
    }
    try {
      const reminded = await sendExpiryReminders();
      logger.info('Expiry reminders processed', { count: reminded });
    } catch (error) {
      logger.error('Error sending expiry reminders', { error });
    }
  } finally {
    isSubscriptionJobRunning = false;
  }
}

async function runPaymentExpiry() {
  if (isPaymentJobRunning) {
    logger.warn('Skipping payment cron: previous run still in progress');
    return;
  }
  isPaymentJobRunning = true;
  try {
    logger.info('Running 5-minute payment expiry checks...');
    const expired = await expirePendingPayments();
    logger.info('Pending payments expired', { count: expired });
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('Error in payment expiry cron', { error });
  } finally {
    isPaymentJobRunning = false;
  }
}

export function startCronJobs() {
  if (env.NODE_ENV === 'test') return;
  if (tasks.length > 0) return; // idempotent

  logger.info('Cron jobs initialized.', { timezone: TIMEZONE });

  tasks = [
    cron.schedule('0 * * * *', runSubscriptionChecks, { timezone: TIMEZONE }),
    cron.schedule('*/5 * * * *', runPaymentExpiry, { timezone: TIMEZONE }),
  ];

  return tasks;
}

export function stopCronJobs() {
  for (const task of tasks) task.stop();
  tasks = [];
}
```

`logger.util.js` has a bug that silently discards every error the cron jobs log, and `cron.service.js` has a failure-isolation problem that means one broken job blocks the other. Both are worth fixing together.

## The headline: `logger.error('msg', error)` drops the error

Winston merges the second argument into the log info object with `Object.assign`. An `Error` instance has **no own enumerable properties** — `message`, `stack`, and `name` are all non-enumerable — so nothing is copied. The error vanishes.

Every failure path in `cron.service.js` uses this form:

```js
logger.error('Error in hourly subscription cron:', error);
```

So when `expireDueSubscriptions` throws, the log line is `Error in hourly subscription cron:` with no stack, no message, no cause. You would have no way to diagnose a failing cron from logs. The fix is `logger.error('...', { error })`, which puts the error in an enumerable property that the formatter can read.

## Second: production removes the only log sink a container has

```js
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {
  logger.remove(logger.transports.Console);
  ...
}
```

You have a `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`. In a container, `docker logs` reads **stdout** — the file transports write to the container's ephemeral filesystem, which is lost on restart and invisible to `docker logs`. So in production you get zero observable logs. Console must stay.

## Third: `level: 'debug'` is hardcoded

Production writes debug-level lines to `combined.log` with no rotation, so the file grows unbounded. Level should come from the environment.

## Fourth: `simple()` format drops meta and has no timestamp

`winston.format.simple()` prints only `level: message`. Even after fixing the `{ error }` call, the console output would still omit it. And there are no timestamps, which makes correlating cron runs impossible.

backend/src/utils/logger.util.js
```
import winston from 'winston';

const isProduction = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production';
const level = process.env.LOG_LEVEL || (isProduction ? 'info' : 'debug');

const consoleFormat = winston.format.combine(
  winston.format.timestamp(),
  winston.format.errors({ stack: true }),
  winston.format.printf(({ timestamp, level: lvl, message, stack, error, ...meta }) => {
    const parts = [`${timestamp} ${lvl}: ${message}`];
    if (stack) parts.push(stack);
    if (error) parts.push(error.stack || String(error));
    if (Object.keys(meta).length > 0) parts.push(JSON.stringify(meta));
    return parts.join(' ');
  })
);

const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level,
  exitOnError: false,
  format: winston.format.combine(
    winston.format.timestamp(),
    winston.format.errors({ stack: true }),
    winston.format.json()
  ),
  transports: [
    new winston.transports.Console({ format: consoleFormat }),
  ],
});

if (isProduction) {
  logger.add(
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: 'error.log',
      level: 'error',
      format: winston.format.json(),
    })
  );
  logger.add(
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: 'combined.log',
      format: winston.format.json(),
    })
  );
}

export default logger;
```

## `cron.service.js`: one failure blocks the other

`expireDueSubscriptions()` and `sendExpiryReminders()` run sequentially inside a single `try`. If expiry throws — and it will, given `AUDIT_ACTIONS.SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED` is `undefined` and `AuditLog.action` is non-nullable — **reminders never run**. The two jobs are independent and should fail independently.

I also added: stored task handles with a `stopCronJobs()` for graceful shutdown, an idempotency guard so a double `startCronJobs()` call doesn't double-schedule, an explicit timezone, and a warning when a run is skipped due to overlap.

backend/src/services/cron.service.js
```
import cron from 'node-cron';
import { expireDueSubscriptions, sendExpiryReminders } from './subscription.service.js';
import { expirePendingPayments } from './payment.service.js';
import { env } from '../config/env.js';
import logger from '../utils/logger.util.js';

const TIMEZONE = process.env.CRON_TIMEZONE || 'UTC';

let isSubscriptionJobRunning = false;
let isPaymentJobRunning = false;
let tasks = [];

async function runSubscriptionChecks() {
  if (isSubscriptionJobRunning) {
    logger.warn('Skipping subscription cron: previous run still in progress');
    return;
  }

  isSubscriptionJobRunning = true;
  try {
    logger.info('Running hourly subscription checks...');

    try {
      const expired = await expireDueSubscriptions();
      logger.info('Expired subscriptions processed', { count: expired });
    } catch (error) {
      logger.error('Error expiring subscriptions', { error });
    }

    try {
      const reminded = await sendExpiryReminders();
      logger.info('Expiry reminders processed', { count: reminded });
    } catch (error) {
      logger.error('Error sending expiry reminders', { error });
    }
  } finally {
    isSubscriptionJobRunning = false;
  }
}

async function runPaymentExpiry() {
  if (isPaymentJobRunning) {
    logger.warn('Skipping payment cron: previous run still in progress');
    return;
  }

  isPaymentJobRunning = true;
  try {
    logger.info('Running 5-minute payment expiry checks...');
    const expired = await expirePendingPayments();
    logger.info('Pending payments expired', { count: expired });
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('Error in payment expiry cron', { error });
  } finally {
    isPaymentJobRunning = false;
  }
}

export function startCronJobs() {
  if (env.NODE_ENV === 'test') {
    return [];
  }

  if (tasks.length > 0) {
    return tasks;
  }

  logger.info('Cron jobs initialized.', { timezone: TIMEZONE });

  tasks = [
    cron.schedule('0 * * * *', runSubscriptionChecks, { timezone: TIMEZONE }),
    cron.schedule('*/5 * * * *', runPaymentExpiry, { timezone: TIMEZONE }),
  ];

  return tasks;
}

export function stopCronJobs() {
  for (const task of tasks) {
    task.stop();
  }
  tasks = [];
}
```

## Two things I could not verify

**`../config/env.js` may not exist at that path.** Your file summary listed it as `src\config\env.js` — at the repo root, not under `backend\`. `cron.service.js` imports `../config/env.js`, which resolves to `backend/src/config/env.js`. If the file really is at the root, this import throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and the server never starts. Add `backend/src/config/env.js` to the chat and I'll confirm.

**`expirePendingPayments` is unverified.** `payment.service.js` is not in the chat, so I can't confirm the export name or that it returns a count. If it returns `undefined`, the log line reads `count: undefined` — harmless, but the name must match or the import fails at startup.

## The multi-instance problem this exposes

The `isSubscriptionJobRunning` guard is **per-process**. If you run more than one replica (docker-compose with `--scale`, or a rolling deploy with overlap), each replica runs its own cron. Combined with `sendExpiryReminders` being non-idempotent — there is no `reminderSentAt` column, so it re-notifies everyone in the window on every run — users get **N reminders per hour**, where N is your replica count.

The in-process guard cannot fix this. It needs either a database-level claim (`reminderSentAt` stamped inside a transaction) or a distributed lock. That is the same `Subscription.reminderSentAt` migration I flagged earlier, and it is now a correctness issue rather than a nice-to-have.

- `backend/prisma/migrations/` — the schema-vs-service question that underlies most of the above.

backend/src/services/zarinpal.service.js
```
import axios from 'axios';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import logger from '../utils/logger.util.js';

const ZARINPAL_CODES = {
  SUCCESS: 100,
  ALREADY_VERIFIED: 101,
};

function getConfig() {
  const merchantId = process.env.ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID;
  if (!merchantId) {
    throw new AppError(500, 'CONFIG_ERROR', 'ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID is not set');
  }

  const sandbox = String(process.env.ZARINPAL_SANDBOX).toLowerCase() === 'true';
  const baseUrl = sandbox
    ? 'https://sandbox.zarinpal.com/pg/v4/payment'
    : 'https://api.zarinpal.com/pg/v4/payment';
  const startPayBase = sandbox
    ? 'https://sandbox.zarinpal.com/pg/StartPay'
    : 'https://www.zarinpal.com/pg/StartPay';

  return { merchantId, baseUrl, startPayBase };
}

function extractError(response) {
  const errors = response?.data?.errors;
  if (Array.isArray(errors) && errors.length > 0) {
    const first = errors[0];
    return {
      code: first?.code,
      message: first?.message || 'Zarinpal request failed',
    };
  }
  return { code: undefined, message: 'Zarinpal request failed' };
}

/**
 * Request a new payment from Zarinpal.
 *
 * @param {Object} params
 * @param {number} params.amount        Amount in Rials (Zarinpal v4 default unit).
 * @param {string} params.callbackUrl   URL Zarinpal redirects the user back to.
 * @param {string} [params.description] Payment description shown to the user.
 * @param {string} [params.email]       Optional payer email.
 * @param {string} [params.mobile]      Optional payer mobile number.
 * @returns {Promise<{ authority: string, paymentUrl: string, fee: number }>}
 */
export async function requestPayment({ amount, callbackUrl, description, email, mobile }) {
  if (!amount || Number(amount) <= 0) {
    throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'amount must be a positive number');
  }
  if (!callbackUrl) {
    throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'callbackUrl is required');
  }

  const { merchantId, baseUrl, startPayBase } = getConfig();

  const payload = {
    merchant_id: merchantId,
    amount: Math.round(Number(amount)),
    callback_url: callbackUrl,
    description: description || 'پرداخت اشتراک',
  };

  const metadata = {};
  if (email) metadata.email = email;
  if (mobile) metadata.mobile = mobile;
  if (Object.keys(metadata).length > 0) payload.metadata = metadata;

  let response;
  try {
    response = await axios.post(`${baseUrl}/request.json`, payload, {
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json' },
      timeout: 15000,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('Zarinpal requestPayment network error:', error?.message);
    throw new AppError(502, 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR', 'خطا در ارتباط با درگاه پرداخت');
  }

  const data = response?.data?.data;
  if (!data || data.code !== ZARINPAL_CODES.SUCCESS || !data.authority) {
    const { code, message } = extractError(response);
    logger.error('Zarinpal requestPayment failed:', { code, message });
    throw new AppError(502, 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR', message, { code });
  }

  return {
    authority: data.authority,
    paymentUrl: `${startPayBase}/${data.authority}`,
    fee: data.fee ?? 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Verify a payment with Zarinpal.
 *
 * @param {Object} params
 * @param {number} params.amount     Amount in Rials (must match the request amount).
 * @param {string} params.authority  Authority returned by Zarinpal on callback.
 * @returns {Promise<{ refId: string, cardPan: string|null, code: number }>}
 */
export async function verifyPayment({ amount, authority }) {
  if (!amount || Number(amount) <= 0) {
    throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'amount must be a positive number');
  }
  if (!authority) {
    throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'authority is required');
  }

  const { merchantId, baseUrl } = getConfig();

  const payload = {
    merchant_id: merchantId,
    amount: Math.round(Number(amount)),
    authority,
  };

  let response;
  try {
    response = await axios.post(`${baseUrl}/verify.json`, payload, {
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json' },
      timeout: 15000,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('Zarinpal verifyPayment network error:', error?.message);
    throw new AppError(502, 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR', 'خطا در ارتباط با درگاه پرداخت');
  }

  const data = response?.data?.data;
  const code = data?.code;

  if (code !== ZARINPAL_CODES.SUCCESS && code !== ZARINPAL_CODES.ALREADY_VERIFIED) {
    const { code: errCode, message } = extractError(response);
    logger.error('Zarinpal verifyPayment failed:', { code: errCode, message });
    throw new AppError(400, 'PAYMENT_VERIFICATION_FAILED', message, { code: errCode });
  }

  return {
    refId: String(data.ref_id),
    cardPan: data.card_pan ?? null,
    code,
  };
}

export default { requestPayment, verifyPayment };
```

export function toPublicPayment(payment) {
  if (!payment) return null;
  return {
    id: payment.id,
    planId: payment.planId,
    planName: payment.plan?.name ?? null,
    amountToman: payment.amountToman,
    status: payment.status,
    refId: payment.refId ?? null,
    cardPanMasked: payment.cardPanMasked ?? null,
    createdAt: payment.createdAt,
    verifiedAt: payment.verifiedAt ?? null,
  };
}

createPaymentRequest(userId, { planId, durationDays }, req):
```js
export async function createPaymentRequest(userId, { planId, durationDays }, req) {
  const plan = await prisma.plan.findUnique({ where: { id: Number(planId) } });
  if (!plan || !plan.isActive) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'پلن یافت نشد');

  const days = Number(durationDays) > 0 ? Number(durationDays) : (plan.duration ?? DEFAULT_DURATION_DAYS);
  const amountToman = Math.round(Number(plan.price));
  if (!amountToman || amountToman <= 0) throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'قیمت پلن نامعتبر است');

  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!user) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'کاربر یافت نشد');

  const payment = await prisma.payment.create({
    data: {
      userId,
      planId: plan.id,
      amountToman,
      durationDays: days,
      status: 'PENDING',
    },
  });

  const callbackUrl = `${getApiBaseUrl()}/api/payments/callback`;

  let gateway;
  try {
    gateway = await requestPayment({
      amount: amountToman * TOMAN_TO_RIAL,
      callbackUrl,
      description: `خرید ${plan.name}`,
      email: user.email,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    await prisma.payment.update({ where: { id: payment.id }, data: { status: 'FAILED' } });
    throw error;
  }

  const updated = await prisma.payment.update({
    where: { id: payment.id },
    data: { authority: gateway.authority },
  });

  await logEvent({ userId, action: 'PAYMENT_CREATED', entity: 'Payment', entityId: payment.id, req });

  return {
    payment: toPublicPayment(updated),
    paymentUrl: gateway.paymentUrl,
    authority: gateway.authority,
  };
}
```

handleCallback({ authority, status }, req):
```js
export async function handleCallback({ authority, status }, req) {
  if (!authority) throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'authority الزامی است');

  const payment = await prisma.payment.findUnique({ where: { authority }, include: { plan: true } });
  if (!payment) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'پرداخت یافت نشد');

  // Idempotency: already finalized
  if (payment.status === 'COMPLETED') {
    return { payment: toPublicPayment(payment), alreadyProcessed: true };
  }
  if (payment.status === 'FAILED') {
    throw new AppError(409, 'CONFLICT', 'این پرداخت قبلا ناموفق ثبت شده است');
  }

  if (status && String(status).toUpperCase() !== 'OK') {
    await failPayment(payment, 'GATEWAY_CANCELLED', req);
    throw new AppError(400, 'PAYMENT_CANCELLED', 'پرداخت توسط کاربر لغو شد');
  }

  let verification;
  try {
    verification = await verifyPayment({
      amount: payment.amountToman * TOMAN_TO_RIAL,
      authority,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    await failPayment(payment, 'VERIFICATION_FAILED', req);
    throw error;
  }

  return finalizePayment(payment, verification, req);
}
```

finalizePayment does the transaction with idempotency guard:

```js
async function finalizePayment(payment, verification, req) {
  const result = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    // Re-read inside the transaction to guard against concurrent callbacks
    const current = await tx.payment.findUnique({ where: { id: payment.id } });
    if (!current) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'پرداخت یافت نشد');
    if (current.status === 'COMPLETED') {
      return { payment: current, alreadyProcessed: true };
    }
    if (current.status !== 'PENDING') {
      throw new AppError(409, 'CONFLICT', 'وضعیت پرداخت قابل تغییر نیست');
    }

    const subscription = await activateSubscription(tx, {
      userId: current.userId,
      planId: current.planId,
      durationDays: current.durationDays,
    });

    const updated = await tx.payment.update({
      where: { id: current.id },
      data: {
        status: 'COMPLETED',
        refId: verification.refId,
        cardPanMasked: maskCardPan(verification.cardPan),
        verifiedAt: new Date(),
        subscriptionId: subscription.id,
      },
    });

    return { payment: updated, subscription, alreadyProcessed: false };
  }, { isolationLevel: 'Serializable' });
  ...
}
```

Hmm, `isolationLevel: 'Serializable'` — Prisma supports it for PostgreSQL. But it can throw serialization errors. Maybe use default isolation with the re-read guard. Actually the re-read inside a transaction with default ReadCommitted doesn't prevent double-activation. Better: use a conditional update as the guard:

```js
const claimed = await tx.payment.updateMany({
  where: { id: current.id, status: 'PENDING' },
  data: { status: 'PROCESSING' },
});
if (claimed.count === 0) { ... already processed ... }
```

But 'PROCESSING' isn't in the PaymentStatus enum. I could add it. Hmm, adding enum value = schema change again. Alternatively use `updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'PENDING' }, data: { status: 'COMPLETED', ... } })` and check count — that's an atomic compare-and-set! Then if count === 0, someone else already completed it → return idempotent result.

But we need the subscription activated too, and the subscription id in the payment update. Order: activate subscription first, then CAS the payment. If CAS fails (concurrent), we'd have double-activated. Hmm.

Better order: CAS the payment to COMPLETED first (with refId etc., subscriptionId null), then activate subscription, then set subscriptionId. If CAS fails → already processed, return. That's atomic and safe. But if activation fails, the transaction rolls back — good, since it's all in one transaction.

So:
```js
const claimed = await tx.payment.updateMany({
  where: { id: payment.id, status: 'PENDING' },
  data: {
    status: 'COMPLETED',
    refId: verification.refId,
    cardPanMasked: maskCardPan(verification.cardPan),
    verifiedAt: new Date(),
  },
});

if (claimed.count === 0) {
  const existing = await tx.payment.findUnique({ where: { id: payment.id } });
  return { payment: existing, alreadyProcessed: true };
}

const subscription = await activateSubscription(tx, {...});

const updated = await tx.payment.update({
  where: { id: payment.id },
  data: { subscriptionId: subscription.id },
});
return { payment: updated, subscription, alreadyProcessed: false };
```

Wait: `updateMany` with `where: { id, status: 'PENDING' }` — Prisma allows non-unique filters in updateMany. Yes.

But there's a subtlety: within a transaction, the updateMany takes a row lock; a concurrent transaction doing the same will block until commit, then see status != PENDING and count 0. Good — that's proper idempotency.

expirePendingPayments():
```js
export async function expirePendingPayments() {
  const cutoff = new Date(Date.now() - PENDING_PAYMENT_TTL_MINUTES * 60 * 1000);
  const result = await prisma.payment.updateMany({
    where: { status: 'PENDING', createdAt: { lt: cutoff } },
    data: { status: 'FAILED' },
  });
  if (result.count > 0) logger.info(`Expired ${result.count} pending payment(s).`);
  return result.count;
}
```

failPayment helper:
```js
async function failPayment(payment, reason, req) {
  const result = await prisma.payment.updateMany({
    where: { id: payment.id, status: 'PENDING' },
    data: { status: 'FAILED' },
  });
  if (result.count === 0) return false;
  await logEvent({ userId: payment.userId, action: 'PAYMENT_FAILED', entity: 'Payment', entityId: payment.id, req });
  logger.warn(`Payment ${payment.id} failed: ${reason}`);
  return true;
}
```

maskCardPan:
```js
function maskCardPan(cardPan) {
  if (!cardPan) return null;
  const digits = String(cardPan).replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (digits.length < 10) return null;
  return `${digits.slice(0, 6)}******${digits.slice(-4)}`;
}
```
