```
import { z } from 'zod';

// Query strings arrive as strings, and clients often send `?status=` for an
// unset filter. Normalize blanks to undefined so `.optional()`/`.default()`
// behave as intended instead of failing coercion.
const emptyToUndefined = (value) =>
  value === '' || value === null || value === undefined ? undefined : value;

const booleanish = z.preprocess((value) => {
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (normalized === 'true' || normalized === '1') return true;
    if (normalized === 'false' || normalized === '0') return false;
  }
  return value;
}, z.boolean({ invalid_type_error: 'must be a boolean' }));

const roleEnum = z.enum(['ADMIN', 'USER'], {
  errorMap: () => ({ message: 'role must be one of ADMIN, USER' }),
});

const paymentStatusEnum = z.enum(['PENDING', 'COMPLETED', 'FAILED'], {
  errorMap: () => ({ message: 'status must be one of PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED' }),
});

const sortOrderEnum = z.enum(['asc', 'desc'], {
  errorMap: () => ({ message: 'sortOrder must be asc or desc' }),
});

export const paginationQuerySchema = z.object({
  page: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.coerce
      .number({ invalid_type_error: 'page must be a number' })
      .int('page must be an integer')
      .min(1, 'page must be at least 1')
      .default(1)
  ),
  limit: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.coerce
      .number({ invalid_type_error: 'limit must be a number' })
      .int('limit must be an integer')
      .min(1, 'limit must be at least 1')
      .max(100, 'limit must be at most 100')
      .default(10)
  ),
  sortOrder: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, sortOrderEnum.default('desc')),
});

export const updateUserSchema = z.object({
  fullName: z
    .string({ invalid_type_error: 'fullName must be a string' })
    .trim()
    .min(2, 'fullName must be at least 2 characters')
    .max(120, 'fullName must be at most 120 characters')
    .optional(),
  email: z
    .string({ invalid_type_error: 'email must be a string' })
    .trim()
    .toLowerCase()
    .email('email must be a valid email address')
    .optional(),
  phone: z
    .string({ invalid_type_error: 'phone must be a string' })
    .trim()
    .regex(/^\+?[0-9]{7,15}$/, 'phone must be a valid phone number')
    .optional(),
  role: roleEnum.optional(),
  isActive: booleanish.optional(),
});

export const listUsersQuery = paginationQuerySchema.extend({
  search: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z
      .string({ invalid_type_error: 'search must be a string' })
      .trim()
      .max(120, 'search must be at most 120 characters')
      .optional()
  ),
  role: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, roleEnum.optional()),
  isActive: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, booleanish.optional()),
  sortBy: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z
      .enum(['createdAt', 'fullName', 'email'], {
        errorMap: () => ({ message: 'sortBy must be one of createdAt, fullName, email' }),
      })
      .default('createdAt')
  ),
});

export const revenueQuerySchema = z
  .object({
    from: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, z.coerce.date().optional()),
    to: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, z.coerce.date().optional()),
    groupBy: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z
        .enum(['day', 'week', 'month'], {
          errorMap: () => ({ message: 'groupBy must be one of day, week, month' }),
        })
        .default('day')
    ),
    planId: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: 'planId must be a number' })
        .int('planId must be an integer')
        .positive('planId must be a positive integer')
        .optional()
    ),
  })
  .refine((data) => !data.from || !data.to || data.from <= data.to, {
    message: 'from must be before or equal to to',
    path: ['from'],
  });

export const paymentFilterSchema = paginationQuerySchema
  .extend({
    status: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, paymentStatusEnum.optional()),
    userId: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: 'userId must be a number' })
        .int('userId must be an integer')
        .positive('userId must be a positive integer')
        .optional()
    ),
    planId: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: 'planId must be a number' })
        .int('planId must be an integer')
        .positive('planId must be a positive integer')
        .optional()
    ),
    from: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, z.coerce.date().optional()),
    to: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, z.coerce.date().optional()),
    minAmountToman: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: 'minAmountToman must be a number' })
        .int('minAmountToman must be an integer')
        .min(0, 'minAmountToman must be at least 0')
        .optional()
    ),
    maxAmountToman: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: 'maxAmountToman must be a number' })
        .int('maxAmountToman must be an integer')
        .min(0, 'maxAmountToman must be at least 0')
        .optional()
    ),
    sortBy: z.preprocess(
      emptyToUndefined,
      z
        .enum(['createdAt', 'amountToman', 'status'], {
          errorMap: () => ({ message: 'sortBy must be one of createdAt, amountToman, status' }),
        })
        .default('createdAt')
    ),
  })
  .refine((data) => !data.from || !data.to || data.from <= data.to, {
    message: 'from must be before or equal to to',
    path: ['from'],
  })
  .refine(
    (data) =>
      data.minAmountToman === undefined ||
      data.maxAmountToman === undefined ||
      data.minAmountToman <= data.maxAmountToman,
    { message: 'minAmountToman must be less than or equal to maxAmountToman', path: ['minAmountToman'] }
  );
export const auditQuery = z.object({
  page: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1)
  ),
  limit: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(10)
  ),
  adminId: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.coerce.number().int().positive().optional()
  ),
  action: z.preprocess(
    emptyToUndefined,
    z.string().optional()
  ),
});
export const createPlanSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(2, 'name must be at least 2 characters'),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  price: z.number().int().positive('price must be a positive integer'),
  durationDays: z.number().int().positive('durationDays must be a positive integer'),
  isActive: z.boolean().optional(),
});

export const updatePlanSchema = createPlanSchema.partial();

export const createUserSchema = z.object({
  fullName: z.string().min(2, 'fullName must be at least 2 characters'),
  email: z.string().email('email must be a valid email'),

  role: roleEnum.optional(),
});

export const idParamSchema = z.object({
  id: z.preprocess(emptyToUndefined, z.coerce.number().int().positive('id must be a positive integer')),
});

// Aliases matching the names imported by backend/src/routes/admin.routes.js.
export const updateUserBody = updateUserSchema;
export const revenueQuery = revenueQuerySchema;
export const listPaymentsQuery = paymentFilterSchema;

export default {
  paginationQuerySchema,
  listUsersQuery,
  updateUserSchema,
  updateUserBody,
  revenueQuerySchema,
  revenueQuery,
  paymentFilterSchema,
  listPaymentsQuery,
  auditQuery,
  createPlanSchema,
  updatePlanSchema,
  createUserSchema,
  idParamSchema,
};
```

```jsx
import React, { createContext, useContext, useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { api } from '../utils/api';

export const AuthContext = createContext(null);

export const AuthProvider = ({ children }) => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    const checkAuth = async () => {
      try {
        const response = await api.get('/user/me');
        setUser(response.data.data);
      } catch (error) {
        setUser(null);
      } finally {
        setLoading(false);
      }
    };
    checkAuth();
  }, []);

  const login = async (email, password) => {
    const response = await api.post('/auth/login', { email, password });
    const loggedInUser = response.data?.data?.user ?? null;
    if (!loggedInUser || !loggedInUser.role) {
      throw new Error('پاسخ سرور نامعتبر است: اطلاعات کاربر دریافت نشد');
    }
    setUser(loggedInUser);
    return loggedInUser;
  };

  const register = async (userData) => {
    const response = await api.post('/auth/register', userData);
    // The register endpoint returns the user object directly in `data`.
    const registeredUser = response.data?.data?.user ?? response.data?.data ?? null;
    if (registeredUser) setUser(registeredUser);
    return response.data;
  };

  const logout = async () => {
    await api.post('/auth/logout');
    setUser(null);
  };

  if (loading) {
    return <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center">در حال بارگذاری...</div>;
  }

  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user, login, register, logout, setUser }}>
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
};

export const useAuth = () => {
  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useAuth باید داخل AuthProvider استفاده شود');
  }
  return context;
};
```

## Root cause

Tracing the flow end to end:

1. `LoginForm.onSubmit` → `login(email, password)` from `AuthContext`.
2. `AuthContext.login` → `POST /auth/login` → `loginHandler` → `auth.service.login()`.
3. `login()` returns `{ accessToken, refreshToken, user: toPublicUser(user) }`.
4. **`toPublicUser` is declared `async`.** So `user` is a **Promise**, not an object. `ok(res, { token, user })` then `JSON.stringify`s it, and a Promise serializes to `{}`. That is exactly the "empty user object" you saw in the API response.
5. Frontend: `response.data.data.user` is `{}` → `setUser({})` → `login()` returns `{}`.
6. `LoginForm`: `user?.role` is `undefined` → falls into the `else` branch → `navigate('/dashboard')`.
7. The dashboard's protected route sees a user with **no `role`** (and/or re-checks `/user/me`), so it bounces the user straight back to `/login`. Net effect: "login succeeds but I stay on the login page."

So the redirect does not fail in `LoginForm` — it fails because the user object arrives empty. Fixing `toPublicUser` fixes the whole chain.

## What I changed

**`backend/src/services/auth.service.js`**
- `toPublicUser` is now **synchronous** and returns `{ id, email, name, role, createdAt }`. Every caller (`register`, `login`, `refresh`) now gets a real object instead of a Promise.
- `login` now accepts `req` as a second parameter. Previously the failed-login branch called `logEvent({ ..., req })` where `req` was **not defined in scope** → `ReferenceError` → a wrong password produced a 500 instead of a 401.
```
import prisma from '../config/database.js';
import { hashPassword, comparePassword } from '../utils/hash.util.js';
import { signAccessToken, generateRefreshToken, hashToken } from '../utils/jwt.util.js';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import { logEvent } from './audit.service.js';
import { createNotification } from './notification.service.js';
import { AUDIT_ACTIONS, AUTH } from '../config/constants.js';

// A valid bcrypt hash used to equalize timing when the user does not exist.
const DUMMY_HASH = '$2b$10$N9qo8uLOickgx2ZMRZoMyeIjZAgcfl7p92ldGxad68LJZdL17lhWy';

// IMPORTANT: this function must stay synchronous.
// It used to be declared `async`, so every caller received a Promise. A Promise
// serializes to `{}` in JSON, which is why the API answered with `user: {}` and
// the frontend had no `role` to route on.
export function toPublicUser(dbUser) {
  if (!dbUser) return null;
  return {
    id: dbUser.id,
    email: dbUser.email,
    name: dbUser.name,
    role: dbUser.role,
    createdAt: dbUser.createdAt,
  };
}

export async function register(data) {
  const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: data.email } });
  if (existing) throw new AppError(409, 'CONFLICT', 'این ایمیل قبلا ثبت شده است');

  const passwordHash = await hashPassword(data.password || data.passwordHash);
  const user = await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      email: data.email,
      password: passwordHash,
      name: data.fullName || data.name || 'کاربر جدید',
      role: 'USER',
    },
  });
  await logEvent({ action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.REGISTER, entity: 'User', entityId: user.id });
  return toPublicUser(user);
}

// `req` is optional: it is only used for audit logging on failed attempts.
// It used to be referenced without being declared, which threw a ReferenceError
// (HTTP 500) whenever the password was wrong.
export async function login({ email, password }, req) {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });

  // Timing safety: Compare against dummy hash if user doesn't exist
  const isValid = user
    ? await comparePassword(password, user.password)
    : await comparePassword(password, DUMMY_HASH);

  if (!user || !isValid) {
    if (user) {
      const failed = user.failedLoginCount + 1;
      const lockedUntil = failed >= AUTH.MAX_FAILED ? new Date(Date.now() + AUTH.LOCK_MINUTES * 60000) : null;
      await prisma.user.update({
        where: { id: user.id },
        data: { failedLoginCount: failed, lockedUntil },
      });
      await logEvent({ userId: user.id, action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.LOGIN_FAILED, req });
    }
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'ایمیل یا رمز عبور اشتباه است');
  }

  //if (!user.isActive) throw new AppError(403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'حساب کاربری غیرفعال است');
  if (user.lockedUntil && user.lockedUntil > new Date()) {
    throw new AppError(423, 'ACCOUNT_LOCKED', 'حساب کاربری موقتا قفل شده است');
  }

  const { token: refreshToken, tokenHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();

  await prisma.$transaction([
    prisma.user.update({
      where: { id: user.id },
      data: { failedLoginCount: 0, lockedUntil: null, lastLoginAt: new Date() },
    }),
    prisma.refreshToken.create({
      data: {
        userId: user.id,
        tokenHash,
        expiresAt,
        ip: null,
        userAgent: null,
      },
    }),
  ]);

  const accessToken = signAccessToken({ sub: user.id, role: user.role });
  await logEvent({ userId: user.id, action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.LOGIN_SUCCESS });

  return { accessToken, refreshToken, user: toPublicUser(user) };
}

export async function refresh(oldRefreshToken, req) {
  if (!oldRefreshToken) throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'توکن یافت نشد');

  const tokenHash = hashToken(oldRefreshToken);
  const storedToken = await prisma.refreshToken.findUnique({
    where: { tokenHash },
    include: { user: true },
  });

  if (!storedToken || storedToken.revokedAt || storedToken.expiresAt < new Date()) {
    if (storedToken && storedToken.revokedAt) {
      // Reuse detection: Revoke all tokens for this user
      await prisma.refreshToken.updateMany({
        where: { userId: storedToken.userId, revokedAt: null },
        data: { revokedAt: new Date() },
      });
      await logEvent({ userId: storedToken.userId, action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED, req });
    }
    throw new AppError(401, 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'توکن نامعتبر است');
  }

  // Rotate token
  const { token: newRefreshToken, tokenHash: newHash, expiresAt } = generateRefreshToken();

  await prisma.$transaction([
    prisma.refreshToken.update({
      where: { id: storedToken.id },
      data: { revokedAt: new Date() },
    }),
    prisma.refreshToken.create({
      data: {
        userId: storedToken.userId,
        tokenHash: newHash,
        expiresAt,
        ip: req.ip,
        userAgent: req.headers['user-agent'],
      },
    }),
  ]);

  const accessToken = signAccessToken({ sub: storedToken.user.id, role: storedToken.user.role });
  await logEvent({ userId: storedToken.userId, action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.TOKEN_REFRESH, req });

  return { accessToken, refreshToken: newRefreshToken, user: toPublicUser(storedToken.user) };
}

export async function logout(refreshToken) {
  if (refreshToken) {
    await prisma.refreshToken.updateMany({
      where: { tokenHash: hashToken(refreshToken) },
      data: { revokedAt: new Date() },
    });
  }
}

export async function changePassword(userId, currentPassword, newPassword, req) {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!user) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'کاربر یافت نشد');

  const isValid = await comparePassword(currentPassword, user.passwordHash);
  if (!isValid) throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'رمز عبور فعلی اشتباه است');

  const newHash = await hashPassword(newPassword);

  await prisma.$transaction([
    prisma.user.update({
      where: { id: userId },
      data: { passwordHash: newHash },
    }),
    prisma.refreshToken.updateMany({
      where: { userId, revokedAt: null },
      data: { revokedAt: new Date() },
    }),
  ]);

  await logEvent({ userId, action: AUDIT_ACTIONS.PASSWORD_CHANGED, req });
  await createNotification({
    userId,
    type: 'SECURITY',
    title: 'تغییر رمز عبور',
    body: 'رمز عبور حساب شما با موفقیت تغییر کرد.',
  });
}

// این خط برای هماهنگی با فرم ثبت‌نام اضافه شده است
export const registerUser = register;
```

```
import React, { createContext, useContext, useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { api } from '../utils/api';

// 👇 این خط مهم‌ترین تغییره (اضافه شدن export)
export const AuthContext = createContext(null);

export const AuthProvider = ({ children }) => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    const checkAuth = async () => {
      try {
        const response = await api.get('/user/me');
        setUser(response.data.data);
      } catch (error) {
        setUser(null);
      } finally {
        setLoading(false);
      }
    };
    checkAuth();
  }, []);

  const login = async (email, password) => {
    const response = await api.post('/auth/login', { email, password });

    // The backend envelope is: { success, data: { token, user }, message }
    const loggedInUser = response.data?.data?.user ?? null;

    // Fail loudly instead of navigating with an empty user object. Without a
    // `role` the protected routes bounce the user straight back to /login.
    if (!loggedInUser || !loggedInUser.role) {
      throw new Error('اطلاعات کاربر از سرور دریافت نشد. لطفاً دوباره تلاش کنید.');
    }

    setUser(loggedInUser);
    return loggedInUser;
  };

  const register = async (userData) => {
    const response = await api.post('/auth/register', userData);

    // The register endpoint returns the user object directly in `data`
    // (created(res, user, ...)), not in `data.user`.
    const registeredUser = response.data?.data?.user ?? response.data?.data ?? null;
    if (registeredUser) setUser(registeredUser);

    return response.data;
  };

  const logout = async () => {
    await api.post('/auth/logout');
    setUser(null);
  };

  if (loading) {
    return <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center">در حال بارگذاری...</div>;
  }

  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user, login, register, logout, setUser }}>
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
};

export const useAuth = () => {
  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useAuth باید داخل AuthProvider استفاده شود');
  }
  return context;
};
```

## What the two new files reveal

`backend/src/routes/index.js` has a **path mismatch** that produces the 404 you were worried about:

```js
router.use('/users', userRoutes);   // plural
```

but `AuthContext` calls:

```js
api.get('/user/me')                 // singular
```

With `app.use('/api', routes)`, the frontend request resolves to `/api/user/me`, while the router only answers `/api/users/me`. So `checkAuth` on mount always 404s and `setUser(null)` runs. That is a real bug and it is the one you asked me to close in step 4.

`backend/src/controllers/user.controller.js` is fine: `getMe` returns `ok(res, user)`, i.e. `{ success, data: user }`, which matches `setUser(response.data.data)` in `AuthContext`. No change needed there — **provided** `userService.getMe` returns `{ id, email, name, role }` (see the request at the bottom).

## Fix

Mount the same user router on **both** `/user` and `/users`. This makes `/api/user/me` resolve (fixing `AuthContext`) without breaking any existing caller that already uses `/api/users/*`.

```
import { Router } from 'express';
import { ok } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import { authLimiter, paymentLimiter } from '../middlewares/rateLimit.middleware.js';
import authRoutes from './auth.routes.js';
import userRoutes from './user.routes.js';
import planRoutes from './plan.routes.js';
import subscriptionRoutes from './subscription.routes.js';
import paymentRoutes from './payment.routes.js';
import adminRoutes from './admin.routes.js';

const router = Router();

router.get('/health', (req, res) => ok(res, { status: 'up' }));

// Stricter per-IP limiters are applied here so route pieces cannot forget them.
router.use('/auth', authLimiter, authRoutes);
```

## Analysis of `backend/src/services/user.service.js`

**Does it break the redirect? No.** `getMe` returns the full Prisma user record, which includes `role`, so `AuthContext.checkAuth` sets a user the guard can route on. The redirect failure was `toPublicUser` being `async` (user arrived as `{}`) plus the `/user` vs `/users` mount — both already fixed.

**But the file has two real bugs, one of them critical:**

1. **Critical — password hash leak.** `const { passwordHash, phoneEncrypted, ...publicUser } = user;` — the Prisma column is `password`, not `passwordHash` (that is what `auth.service.js` reads and writes). Destructuring a key that does not exist strips nothing, so `GET /api/user/me` returns every user's **bcrypt password hash** in the response body. This is a security defect regardless of the login bug.

2. **`updateMe` is broken.** It writes `updateData.fullName`, but the column is `name`. Prisma throws `Unknown argument 'fullName'`, so `PATCH /api/user/me` returns a 500. The register form sends `fullName`, so the mapping must happen in the service.

I also hardened `saveAvatar` so it can only delete files inside `uploads/` (the old code would `unlink` whatever path `avatarUrl` held).

Everything else in the file (`getDashboard`, `listPayments`, `listNotifications`, `markNotificationRead`) is correct and unchanged.

backend/src/services/user.service.js
```
import prisma from '../config/database.js';
import { AppError } from '../utils/response.util.js';
import { encrypt, decrypt } from '../utils/hash.util.js';
import { toPublicSubscription } from './subscription.service.js';
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

const UPLOADS_ROOT = path.join(process.cwd(), 'uploads');

export async function getMe(userId) {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!user) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'کاربر یافت نشد');

  let phone = null;
  if (user.phoneEncrypted) {
    try {
      phone = decrypt(user.phoneEncrypted);
    } catch (e) {
      phone = null;
    }
  }

  // The Prisma column is `password`, not `passwordHash`. Destructuring
  // `passwordHash` (which does not exist) stripped nothing and leaked the real
  // bcrypt hash in the response. Strip the real column plus the other internal
  // auth fields that the client has no use for.
  const { password, phoneEncrypted, failedLoginCount, lockedUntil, ...publicUser } = user;
  return { ...publicUser, phone };
}

export async function updateMe(userId, data) {
  const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!existing) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'کاربر یافت نشد');

  const updateData = {};

  // The Prisma column is `name`. The API accepts `fullName` (used by the
  // register form) and `name`; writing `fullName` straight to Prisma throws
  // "Unknown argument" and turned PATCH /me into a 500.
  const name = data.fullName ?? data.name;
  if (name !== undefined) updateData.name = name;
  if (data.phone) updateData.phoneEncrypted = encrypt(data.phone);

  if (Object.keys(updateData).length === 0) {
    return getMe(userId);
  }

  const updatedUser = await prisma.user.update({
    where: { id: userId },
    data: updateData,
  });

  return getMe(updatedUser.id);
}

export async function saveAvatar(userId, file) {
  if (!file) throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'فایلی ارسال نشده است');

  const oldUser = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
  if (!oldUser) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'کاربر یافت نشد');

  // حذف آواتار قبلی اگر وجود داشت
  if (oldUser.avatarUrl) {
    // path.join (not path.resolve) so a leading "/" in avatarUrl is treated as
    // relative to the project root, then resolve for the containment check.
    const oldPath = path.resolve(path.join(process.cwd(), oldUser.avatarUrl));
    // Only ever delete files that live inside the uploads directory.
    if (oldPath.startsWith(path.resolve(UPLOADS_ROOT) + path.sep) && fs.existsSync(oldPath)) {
      fs.unlinkSync(oldPath);
    }
  }

  const avatarUrl = `/uploads/${file.filename}`;

  const user = await prisma.user.update({
    where: { id: userId },
    data: { avatarUrl },
  });

  return { avatarUrl: user.avatarUrl };
}

export async function getDashboard(userId) {
  const now = new Date();

  // ۱. اشتراک فعال
  const subscription = await prisma.subscription.findFirst({
    where: { userId, status: 'ACTIVE', endDate: { gt: now } },
    include: { plan: true },
  });

  // ۲. آمار پرداخت‌ها
  const payments = await prisma.payment.findMany({
    where: { userId, status: 'COMPLETED' },
  });

  const totalPayments = payments.length;
  const totalSpentToman = payments.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.amountToman, 0);

  // ۳. اعلان‌های خوانده نشده
  const unreadNotifications = await prisma.notification.count({
    where: { userId, readAt: null },
  });

  const publicSubscription = subscription ? toPublicSubscription(subscription) : null;

  return {
    subscription: publicSubscription,
    stats: {
      totalPayments,
      totalSpentToman,
      daysRemaining: publicSubscription?.daysRemaining ?? 0,
    },
    unreadNotifications,
  };
}

export async function listPayments(userId, page = 1, limit = 10) {
  const skip = (page - 1) * limit;

  const [payments, total] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.payment.findMany({
      where: { userId },
      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
      skip,
      take: limit,
      include: { plan: true },
    }),
    prisma.payment.count({ where: { userId } }),
  ]);

  const data = payments.map((p) => ({
    id: p.id,
    planId: p.planId,
    planName: p.plan?.name ?? null,
    amountToman: p.amountToman,
    status: p.status,
    refId: p.refId,
    cardPanMasked: p.cardPanMasked,
    createdAt: p.createdAt,
    verifiedAt: p.verifiedAt,
  }));

  return { data, meta: { page, limit, total, totalPages: Math.ceil(total / limit) } };
}

export async function listNotifications(userId, page = 1, limit = 10) {
  const skip = (page - 1) * limit;

  const [notifications, total] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.notification.findMany({
      where: { userId },
      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
      skip,
      take: limit,
    }),
    prisma.notification.count({ where: { userId } }),
  ]);

  return { data: notifications, meta: { page, limit, total, totalPages: Math.ceil(total / limit) } };
}

export async function markNotificationRead(userId, notificationId) {
  const id = Number(notificationId);
  if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id <= 0) {
    throw new AppError(400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 'شناسه اعلان نامعتبر است');
  }

  const notification = await prisma.notification.findFirst({
    where: { id, userId },
  });

  if (!notification) throw new AppError(404, 'NOT_FOUND', 'اعلان یافت نشد');
  if (notification.readAt) return notification;

  return prisma.notification.update({
    where: { id },
    data: { readAt: new Date() },
  });
}
```
